item.title: ASP.NET Core Large File Upload Limit Configuration: IIS, Kestrel, and Application Settings
item.description:
“ASP.NET Core Large File Upload Limit Configuration: IIS, Kestrel, and Application Settings”

When handling file uploads or large data payloads in ASP.NET Core applications, developers frequently encounter limitations on the maximum request body size. These restrictions are imposed at multiple layers: by the hosting environment (like IIS), by the built-in web server (Kestrel), and within the application’s configuration itself via middleware settings. Overcoming these hurdles requires coordinated adjustments across these areas.

item.title: Laravel Remove Public Directory From URL Security and Configuration Methods
item.description:
“Laravel Remove Public Directory From URL Security and Configuration Methods”

When deploying a Laravel application, the entry point is typically the public/index.php file. Accessing the application often requires navigating to http://yourdomain.com/public/. For clean URLs and professional presentation, developers frequently seek ways to make the root of the domain point directly to the application logic without exposing the /public segment. This requires careful manipulation, usually involving .htaccess rules or web server configurations, while maintaining crucial security boundaries.
